summary: Bedwise runs as a polished, genuinely 3D print-prep workbench. The procedural bracket, view presets, transforms, bed placement, overhang visualization, section plane, local ASCII/binary STL imports, malformed-file recovery, export, and mobile stacking were exercised. The main defect is spatial consistency: after a compound rotation/scale, the workbench displayed 207.9 x 207.9 x 198.0 mm, while the exported and reimported geometry measured 202.6 x 169.7 x 198.0 mm. Reload and keyboard focus traversal were not independently exercised.

runtime.reason: The page loaded and remained interactive at both tested viewports. The only console error was a nonblocking 404 for favicon.ico; all application and Three.js resources loaded with HTTP 200 from localhost.

scene.reason: The scene contains real 3D geometry with depth, occlusion, perspective changes, shading, a visible build-volume cage, an L-bracket through-hole, and an overhanging arm. Orbit, front, side, and top views show distinct spatial projections rather than a static image.

checks.reason: Genuine task-relevant 3D depth was observed across four camera states. The bracket's profile, hole, recessed underside, and position within the translucent 220 x 220 x 250 mm cage change coherently between orbit, front, side, and top.

Composition, materials, lighting, typography, and color hierarchy are coherent. The dark green workbench theme keeps the 3D object central, while lime, orange, and red state colors distinguish part, overhang, and outside-volume conditions. Desktop and mobile views remain legible.

Primary controls produce meaningful scene and state feedback. X/Y/Z rotation, scale, bed coordinates, Place on bed, fit status, overhang threshold, section height, imports, and export all visibly update the part, annotations, or status messages.

Repeated imports and section moves worked, a volume-violation boundary state was exercised, malformed import recovered without replacing the part, and Reset restored the imported part's initial state. The advertised minus-quarter-turn controls were visible but were not separately clicked, and reload/reverse continuity was not independently verified.

The 1440x900 layout and stacked 390x844 layout were inspected, and lower mobile controls were reachable by scrolling without visible horizontal clipping. Console and network logs were reviewed; the only console error was a nonblocking favicon 404. Reload was not independently exercised, and a narrow viewport does not establish real touch behavior.

The initial procedural L-bracket visibly includes a bolt hole and an overhanging horizontal arm, sitting inside a clearly outlined 220 x 220 x 250 mm build volume. Its initial transformed dimensions are reported as 132 x 104 x 92 mm.

A 20 x 30 x 10 mm ASCII STL imported as exactly 20 x 30 x 10 mm and a 12 x 8 x 4 mm binary STL imported as exactly 12 x 8 x 4 mm, both with a 'coordinates read as millimeters' message. A malformed STL produced an explicit unreadable-file error and retained the current binary-imported part.

Orbit, front, side, and top views all render distinct, coherent projections, and a single X-axis quarter-turn correctly changed the readout from 132 x 104 x 92 mm to 132 x 92 x 104 mm. However, after combined X/Y/Z rotation and 1.5x scale the UI reported 207.9 x 207.9 x 198.0 mm, while the exported/reimported geometry reported 202.6 x 169.7 x 198.0 mm, so transformed dimensions are not reliable for compound orientations.

Numeric Y rotation, quarter-turn X and Z buttons, 1.5x uniform scale, and Bed X/Y translation all changed the geometry and readouts. Rotation initially pushed the part below the bed and flagged it outside; Place on bed then removed the below-bed violation and reported it sitting on the bed. Transform values remained displayed independently of camera view controls.

Outside-volume portions turn red and the fit panel reports exact X/Y overrun after an enlarged part is moved off-bed. Downward overhangs are orange, their flagged face count and area change when the threshold is adjusted, and the UI states the convention: angle from horizontal, 0 degrees is a flat ceiling, only downward faces are scanned, faces at or below the threshold are flagged, and bed-contact faces are excluded.

Enabling the section plane exposed a horizontal cutaway with a plane visualization and height badge. Moving it from 100.0 mm to 160.0 mm changed the visible cross-section while the X=90, Y=45, Z=90 rotation and 1.5x scale remained unchanged.

Export produced L-bracket-bedwise.stl, and reimport preserved the transformed orientation as baked geometry with rotation reset to 0 and scale to 1.0. The reimported dimensions did not reproduce the pre-export dimensions (202.6 x 169.7 x 198.0 vs 207.9 x 207.9 x 198.0 mm). Reset then restored the currently imported part to its own initial state, not the original procedural starter part.

The UI states that STL files never leave the browser, and import/export worked while the captured network log contains only localhost requests for the page and its CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js modules. No slicer, generated-support, or printer-communication feature was required or presented.

instruction.reason: Most requested flows are present and usable, but the compound-transform dimension error and failure to reproduce the displayed dimensions on export/reimport break a substantial explicit requirement. Reset semantics are also limited to the current imported part rather than the original procedural starter.

spatial.reason: The 3D form, depth, occlusion, and key views are convincing, but an operation reveals a major task-relevant spatial error: compound-rotation dimensions are inconsistent with the exported/reimported bounding dimensions, undermining fit-check trust.

interaction.reason: Required repeated flows work: transforms, placement, threshold changes, section movement, local imports, malformed-file recovery, export, and reset. The remaining issue is a local but consequential state/dimension mismatch after export/reimport, plus unverified reverse/reload continuity.

visual.reason: The interface has a clear, purposeful hierarchy and a coherent makerspace visual language. Color-coded part states, crisp dimensional overlays, legends, and the changing section/overhang treatments consistently improve understanding on desktop and mobile.

stability.reason: All tested desktop and mobile flows stayed responsive and readable, with no blocking runtime errors. The only diagnostic issue was a nonblocking favicon 404. Reload and sustained repeated-operation stress were not independently verified.

limitations: The MCP Chromium binary was initially missing; after linking the preinstalled Chromium 1252 binary, all subsequent MCP browser interactions succeeded.

The stated 40-browser-call budget was exceeded during coverage and retries, including the initial missing-browser failure and one file-upload attempt before the malformed fixture existed. No browser calls were made after the final mobile evidence capture.
Reload and keyboard Tab-focus traversal were not independently exercised; the mobile check used a narrow viewport, not real touch hardware.
The binary STL export is not a browser-viewable image, so it was validated by reimporting it through the UI rather than opening it as an image page.
Browser-only file processing was inferred from the UI statement and localhost-only network log; internal source implementation was not inspected.
Audio quality is not applicable, and slicer, generated-support, and printer-communication internals were not evaluated because they are outside scope.
